channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Afghanistan Launches Nationwide Polio Vaccination Campaign
item.description: Afghanistan Without Polio has initiated a nationwide polio vaccination campaign, urging families to protect their children. The campaign begins in the southern zone on November 3. Afghanistan and Pakistan remain the only countries reporting wild poliovirus cases, with the disease continuing to threaten children's health.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Discuss Transport Cooperation and Smart Zones
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Transport met with a South Korean delegation to discuss cooperation in the transport sector. Five projects worth $7 million, supported by South Korea, are underway or completed. A memorandum of understanding was signed for smart transport development in Dushanbe.

item.title: Seven Agencies Licensed for Kyrgyz Citizen Employment Abroad
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interdepartmental Commission has issued new permits and extended existing ones for seven private employment agencies facilitating overseas work for Kyrgyz citizens. Companies received licenses for destinations including Turkey, Germany, and Poland. The commission denied licenses for employment in Russia and Germany for two other agencies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Business Deposits Grow by Trillion Tenge, Top Banks See Gains
item.description: In September, corporate deposits in Kazakhstan banks increased by 1.2 trillion tenge, reaching 21.5 trillion tenge. Most major banks experienced net deposit growth, although Kaspi Bank and Otbasy Bank saw outflows. Bank CenterCredit saw the largest increase, followed by Halyk Bank and Bank RBK.

item.title: Almaty Reconsiders BRT Project Amidst SkyTrain Monorail Study
item.description: Almaty authorities have paused the BRT line on Raimbek Avenue to study a proposed Almaty SkyTrain monorail project. The city aims to integrate future transit lines and avoid redundant construction. A new traffic scheme is being developed, potentially moving bus lanes to the road edges. The original BRT project, costing nearly 40 billion tenge, began in 2025.

item.title: Kazakh President Visits Temirtau in Karaganda Region
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan is visiting the Karaganda region today. The presidential itinerary includes a visit to several facilities in Temirtau. This visit is part of the head of state's ongoing regional tours.

item.title: Microsoft and Meta Experts Discuss Cooperation with Uzbekistan in Seattle
item.description: An international forum on developing cooperation between Uzbekistan and the US in artificial intelligence was held at the Consulate General of Uzbekistan in Washington. The forum was organized in collaboration with the American-Uzbekistan Business and Investment Council, IT Park Uzbekistan, and the Global Digital Technologies Academy.

item.title: Over $405,000 in Unpaid Wages Returned to Tajik Migrants in Russia
item.description: Tajik labor migrants working in Russia had over 32.5 million rubles (over $405,000) in unpaid wages returned to them in the first ten months of 2026. The representative office of Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor, Migration, and Employment in Russia reported this. Issues cited include lack of written contracts and informal employment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Online Service for Business Credit History Reports
item.description: A new digital service for entrepreneurs has been launched on the eGov Business mobile app in Kazakhstan. Business representatives can now obtain credit and insurance history reports online and for free. The service allows companies to monitor their credit obligations. Three types of reports are available from the State Credit Bureau.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev begins working visit to Karaganda region
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan has arrived in the Karaganda region for a working visit, according to Akorda. During the trip, the head of state will visit several industrial and social facilities in Temirtau and receive information on the region's socio-economic development.

item.title: Eldor Aripov: Central Asia's strategic independence means more choices, not choosing between partners
item.description: Eldor Aripov, director of Uzbekistan's Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies, stated that Central Asia is gaining independent strategic importance, no longer viewed solely through the lens of Russia, China, or Afghanistan. Closer ties with the EU should expand opportunities for markets, investments, and transport, rather than forcing a choice between external partners.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Banking Sector Experiences Rapid Expansion, Assets Reach $14 Billion
item.description: The banking sector in Kyrgyzstan has seen rapid expansion, with total assets increasing by 50% to $14 billion by the end of 2025, according to National Bank Chairman Almaz Baketaev. Assets grew another 24.2% in the first eight months of the current year, with loans comprising about 42% of total assets.

item.title: Gulf Oil Continues Assessing Economic Viability of Uzbekistan Gas Station Network
item.description: American company Gulf Oil is still evaluating the economic feasibility of establishing a network of gas stations in Uzbekistan. Potential sites along major highways have been studied, and the company is currently calculating the project's economic efficiency. Decisions on construction will follow.

item.title: Turkey-Azerbaijan Disagreements Threaten Western-Backed Regional Projects
item.description: Disagreements between Baku and Ankara, highlighted by the absence of Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev at a summit in Ankara, are raising concerns about Western-backed transport and energy projects in the region. Analysts suggest these tensions could slow down project approvals and negotiations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Revokes Licenses of 78 Medical Organizations in Nine Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has revoked licenses from 78 medical organizations, including dental clinics, within the first nine months of the year. The Committee for Medical Control initiated legal proceedings against non-compliant clinics to ensure patient safety and adherence to licensing standards.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Complete 10 Long-Delayed Water Management Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to finalize ten long-standing projects in its water management sector. This initiative aims to address critical infrastructure needs and improve water resource utilization across the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Man Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for Arson Attack on Woman and Children
item.description: A man in Uzbekistan's Kashkadarya region has been sentenced to life in prison for an arson attack that killed two of a woman's four children. The incident occurred in May 2026 when the man doused the woman and her children with gasoline and set them on fire. The woman and two other children survived.

item.title: Iran Dispatches First Export Freight Train to China via Central Asia
item.description: Iran has sent its first container train carrying export goods from Qom province to Xi'an, China. This follows a similar train from China to Iran via Central Asia in September. The train carries approximately 50 containers of bitumen, a petroleum product used in road construction. The new route offers cost and time savings.

item.title: Talas Budget and Investments Skyrocket Over Five Years
item.description: Talas city's budget has increased over fourfold, and investments have grown nearly sixteenfold in the past five years. President Sadyr Japarov was presented with these figures during a working visit. The local budget is projected to reach 947.6 million soms by 2026, up from 224 million in 2021. Industrial output and investments also saw significant increases.

item.title: Over 3,700 Body Cameras Issued to Kyrgyzstan Police Officers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's police force has been equipped with over 3,700 body cameras. These devices are distributed across all regions and are intended to monitor officers' adherence to laws and regulations, and to prevent corruption. Recordings can be used as evidence in disputes, and officers cannot disable the cameras during their shifts.

item.title: Man Arrested for 15 Days in Almaty for Inciting Truckers to Stop
item.description: A 41-year-old man in Almaty has been arrested for 15 days for inciting mass truck stops. He had called on drivers to halt their movement on November 1st to protest restrictions on heavy vehicle traffic. Police identified him through a video appeal shared on social media. The specific charge under Kazakhstan's administrative code was not detailed.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizen Extradited from US for Allegedly Running International Drug Smuggling Ring
item.description: A Kyrgyz citizen has been extradited from the United States to Kyrgyzstan on suspicion of organizing an international drug trafficking channel. Authorities allege he used regular postal parcels, disguised as consumer goods, to send marijuana and psychotropic substances. The operation involved Kyrgyzstan's anti-drug service, the DEA, and Interpol.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Overturns Unlawful Child Support Calculation for Father on Parental Leave
item.description: A private bailiff in Aktobe unlawfully calculated child support for a father on parental leave, deeming him unemployed and overcharging him. The father successfully challenged the decision in court. The court ruled that the bailiff's calculation method was illegal, as the father retained his employment. The bailiff was ordered to recalculate the support based on the father's pre-leave salary.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Restrict Used Car Imports Based on Age and Emission Standards
item.description: Kazakhstan will impose new restrictions on the import of used cars for personal use, limiting them by age and environmental class. The Ministry of Transport is introducing requirements for vehicles imported by individuals, including compliance with Euro-5 emission standards or higher and a maximum vehicle age of five years. These rules will apply to cars, motorcycles, and certain other vehicles.

item.title: Tashkent Families Face Eviction Due to Foreign Heirs Claiming Property Rights
item.description: Several families in Tashkent are at risk of losing their legally purchased homes due to claims from foreign heirs. In one case, a family bought and renovated an apartment, only for a realtor representing a foreign heir to reclaim it through court. Another family faces a similar situation after purchasing a property that was later declared invalid due to a foreign heir's claim.

item.title: Almaty Resident Arrested for Operating Synthetic Drug Lab in Apartment
item.description: A small laboratory for producing synthetic drugs was discovered in an Almaty apartment. Police arrested a 34-year-old resident suspected of organizing the illegal production. The lab was located on the top floor to conceal the odor, utilizing the building's ventilation system. Approximately 4.5 kg of finished product was seized.

item.title: Drug Shop Money Laundering Operation Uncovered in Aktobe
item.description: Authorities in Aktobe have dismantled a criminal group that facilitated payments for an online drug marketplace. The operation processed over 918,000 USDT, equivalent to more than 400 million tenge, through 22 bank cards and cryptocurrency. The organizer has been detained.

item.title: New Enterprises, Schools, and Service Centers Opened in Sughd Region During President Rahmon's Visit
item.description: During his working visit to the Sughd region, President Emomali Rahmon oversaw the opening of several new enterprises, schools, and service centers. The president's visit to the region is ongoing.

item.title: China to Investigate Officials' Families for Unexplained Wealth
item.description: China is implementing new regulations requiring officials to explain the source of their family members' wealth. Relatives' income and assets will be scrutinized, especially if they significantly exceed the official's salary. This measure aims to combat corruption and prevent the abuse of official positions for personal gain.

item.title: Zelensky Claims Russia Suffered Record 54,400 Military Casualties in October
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed Russia sustained 54,400 military casualties in October, the highest monthly figure since the war began. He also stated Ukraine recaptured 96.2 square kilometers of territory. Zelensky described October 21 as a record day for Russian losses. Russia has not yet responded, and independent verification is difficult.

item.title: Bulgarian President Opposed to Military Aid for Ukraine Wins Second Round
item.description: Bulgaria's President Ilina Yotova, who favors dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, has won the second round of the presidential election. She defeated pro-Western politician Andrey Gyurov. The election occurred amid security concerns following drone attacks on Black Sea vessels, which some linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.

item.title: Kazakhstan to establish laboratory for biological forest protection against pests
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to create a specialized laboratory for breeding entomophages to biologically protect forests from pests. The project, approved at the Asian Forest Cooperation Organization assembly, aims to reduce chemical use and improve monitoring systems. It is scheduled for completion between 2027 and 2030.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Receive €103.7 Million for Forest and Pasture Restoration
item.description: The Green Climate Fund has approved a regional program for Central Asia, allocating €103.7 million to Uzbekistan for restoring forests, pastures, and developing sustainable agriculture. The funds will support climate-resilient technologies and improve farmer access to financial tools.

item.title: Russia Strikes Ukrainian Regions, Causing Casualties and Widespread Power Outages
item.description: Russia launched overnight strikes on several Ukrainian regions on November 1, 2026, injuring six in Sumy and four in Rivne. Energy infrastructure was targeted, leaving hundreds of thousands of families without electricity. Ukraine's president stated Russia is attempting to exploit Ukraine's shortage of ballistic missile interceptors.

item.title: Tajikistan and China Sign Protocol for Murgab-Kulma Road Reconstruction
item.description: The Ministry of Transport of Tajikistan and the Chinese Embassy in Dushanbe signed a protocol on the feasibility study for the Murgab-Kulma road reconstruction. The project, funded by Chinese grant aid, will reconstruct 90 km of the road. Construction is expected to begin in 2027. This road is vital for regional transport and trade.

item.title: Prosecutors Protect Investor Rights in Kyzylorda, Kazakhstan
item.description: Prosecutors in Kyzylorda, Kazakhstan, have intervened to protect the rights of an investor, TОО "TEMA RETAILKZ." The city's sanitary-epidemiological control department applied a measure without prior prosecutor approval, which was later revoked. Officials involved face administrative penalties.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Subsidize Utility Bills for Low-Income Households
item.description: Kazakhstan will provide financial assistance to cover a portion of utility costs for households where expenses exceed 5-10% of their income. Approximately 8,000 individuals currently receive housing assistance, with 400 million tenge allocated from local budgets this year. An additional 28 billion tenge is designated for reducing water costs.

item.title: Man Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for Burning Woman and Four Children in Qashqadaryo
item.description: A man has been sentenced to life imprisonment in the Guzar district of Qashqadaryo region for burning a woman and her four children. Two children died as a result of the incident. The court found the defendant guilty of intentional murder with extreme cruelty.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes New Cybersecurity Training System for State Organizations
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced a new system for cybersecurity personnel in state organizations and companies with over 50% state ownership. Specialists will undergo training at Cyber University every two years. Those with recognized foreign certificates are exempt.

item.title: Kazakhstan Housing Company and Bank RBK Partner for Housing Construction Development
item.description: Kazakhstan Housing Company and Bank RBK have signed an agreement to finance comprehensive housing complex construction projects. This partnership will facilitate access to preferential loans for domestic construction companies, focusing on large-scale urban development projects. The initiative aims to reduce financial burdens and improve project efficiency.
